current.text: He picked up his 5 million USD player option and stays in Milwaukee. Experts read this as a sign that no other team wanted him.
Milwaukee has a new head coach, Taylor Jenkins. Doc Rivers, who made Porter his preferred player and gave him big minutes, is gone.

The Milwaukee backcourt is crowded with Rollins, Herro, Burries, Jakucionis, Trent and Green. The projected starters to open the season are Rollins, Herro, Jaquez, Kuzma and Turner, so Porter is not in the projected starting five.
Experts cannot tell how Jenkins will use him. He is projected as a sixth man, and his minutes could land anywhere from 18 to 27.
Experts expect his minutes to be well below last season's 33, and they do not expect him to repeat a top 25 per game season.
Experts do not trust last season's 2.2 steals, 7.4 assists and 88% free throws to repeat. Of last season's steals leaders, he is the most likely to regress a lot.
His efficient scoring came from tough mid-range shots, and experts think that efficiency is unlikely to last.
He looked okay after his knee problems and played in the preseason. Yahoo lists him as questionable for rest.
Experts call him a late-round flyer worth taking around picks 110 to 140. He has top 50 upside if he reaches about 29 minutes, and they would take him over Kuzma or Jaquez.
Milwaukee needs trades to consolidate its roster. Experts say Porter, Kuzma, Jaquez and Herro do not fit well together.
Milwaukee is expected to give young players more minutes as the season goes on, which would cut veteran minutes.

durable.text: He had multiple knee problems last season, likely including more than one surgery.
His game leans on tough mid-range shots, and he takes few threes. That makes 3PM his weakest category for a guard.
Steals are his standout category. His projected steals are far above the top 250 pool, but he was not a steals player before last season.
His FT% is unpredictable. It jumped from 77% to 88% last season, and he has a 60% FT season in his career.
Experts do not rate him as a real-life player. They call him inefficient and ball dominant, even though his fantasy numbers in a big role are strong.

note: He costs almost nothing (Yahoo 3 USD, ESPN 2 USD, 3 USD in our league last season, ranks 130 and 109). That makes him a 1 to 3 USD bench flyer for a punt 3PM build that wants steals and assists from a guard. His 17.4 points, 7.4 assists and 2.2 steals came in 33 minutes over only 38 games. The projections already price him at about 27 minutes as a bench guard. In the first two weeks, check his minutes under Jenkins, whether he passes Rollins or Herro for a starting job, and whether his steal rate holds. If he plays under about 25 minutes, drop him for a waiver option.
